zh: 我勉强还算是个律师。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not practicing.
zh: 你已经不执业了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happened in your life that you found yourself on that farm in Hawaii thinking about putting a first podcast out?
zh: 你的生活中发生了什么,让你发现自己身处夏威夷的一个农场,想着推出第一期播客?

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot happened.
zh: 发生了很多事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I was raised pretty traditionally in a very education-first, achievement-oriented household.
zh: 你知道,我是在一个非常以教育为先、以成就为导向的家庭里相当传统地长大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I was sort of indoctrinated into this philosophy of life that happiness is a product of, you know, climbing the corporate ladder and crafting a safe and secure career for yourself where you were well-paid and you could be kind of a
zh: 所以我某种程度上被灌输了一种人生哲学:幸福是攀爬企业阶梯、为自己打造一份安全稳定职业的产物,在那里你薪酬优厚,可以成为

speaker: Unknown
en: A respected member of society.
zh: 一个受人尊敬的社会成员。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was pretty good at playing that game.
zh: 所以我挺擅长玩那个游戏的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But things started to crack pretty early in that I developed an affinity for alcohol that took me down some dark alleyways and was essentially a functioning alcoholic for maybe 10 years and a really bad alcoholic for five years.
zh: 但很早 things 就开始出现裂痕,因为我养成了对酒精的依赖,把我带入了一些黑暗的小巷,我基本上是一个功能性酗酒者大概十年,然后是一个很糟糕的酗酒者五年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ultimately, I got sober at 31, but it really broke me.
zh: 最终,我在31岁时戒了酒,但它真的把我击垮了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I ended up in a treatment center in Oregon where I spent a hundred days and was introduced to new tools for living.
zh: 我最后进了俄勒冈州的一个治疗中心,在那里待了一百天,并被介绍认识了一些新的生活工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that was the first time that I began to question
zh: 我觉得那是我第一次开始质疑

speaker: Unknown
en: what I was doing with my life because I never really had before.
zh: 我在用自己的生活做什么,因为我之前从来没有真正质疑过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was just on the track, you know?
zh: 我只是一直在那条轨道上,你知道的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you end up there?
zh: 你是怎么落到那一步的?

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you end up in the 100-day rehab?
zh: 你是怎么进那个100天戒瘾中心的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I started drinking in college and it was a pretty, you know, party permissive environment, work hard, play hard.
zh: 我在大学开始喝酒,那是一个相当,你知道的,对派对很宽容的环境,努力工作,尽情玩乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: But from the get go, it was pretty noticeable that I had a different relationship with alcohol than everyone else.
zh: 但从一开始就很明显,我和酒精的关系与其他所有人都不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I was the last guy to leave the party.
zh: 就像我总是派对上最后一个离开的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the keg was tapped out, I was the guy looking for the half empties.
zh: 如果酒桶被喝空了,我就是那个去找半空的酒瓶的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was the guy who ended up doing something stupid that everyone wanted to joke about the next day.
zh: 我是那个最终干了蠢事、第二天所有人都想拿来开玩笑的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's all fun and games when you're 21 years old.
zh: 当你21岁的时候,这些都不算什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then I moved to New York City and I was learning how to become a professional alcoholic there because that is the best place to do that.
zh: 然后我搬到了纽约市,我在那里学习如何成为一个职业酗酒者,因为那是做这件事的最佳地点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I had a great time.
zh: 而且我玩得很开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I was somebody who was living my life in dissonance with my spirit, but I was unaware of that.
zh: 就像,我是一个在生活中与自己的精神相背离的人,但我没有意识到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was just going along my way, but something was wrong, you know, and that relationship with alcohol continued to deepen and worsen, and the consequences for my behavior started to get more and more significant.
zh: 我只是照着自己的方式往前走,但有什么地方不对劲,你知道的,那段与酒精的关系持续加深和恶化,而我行为的后果开始变得越来越严重。

speaker: Unknown
en: To the point where I was living a double life, thinking no one knew what I was doing, but of course they do.
zh: 以至于我过着双重生活,以为没有人知道我在做什么,但当然他们知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I ended up getting in trouble with the law.
zh: 我最终惹上了法律麻烦。

speaker: Unknown
en: I ended up, you know, having difficulty holding down a job.
zh: 我最终,你知道的,很难保住一份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got two DUIs in a period of about six or eight weeks.
zh: 我在大约六到八周的时间里吃了两张 DUI(酒驾)罚单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Shortly after I'd moved to Los Angeles, I was facing jail time.
zh: 在我搬到洛杉矶后不久,我面临着牢狱之灾。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was on the precipice of getting fired from my law firm job.
zh: 而且我处于即将被律师事务所解雇的边缘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my parents finally said, we can't talk to you anymore.
zh: 我父母最后说，我们没办法再跟你谈了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we're here for you if, and when you're ready to get help, but you have a big problem and we're not available to be like codependent in this situation any longer.
zh: 就是，如果你准备好寻求帮助了，或者什么时候准备好了，我们会在你身边，但你有一个很严重的问题，我们不再能在这件事上继续互相依赖了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't have one singular rock bottom moment, but I did have a marriage that went sideways and ended on the honeymoon.
zh: 我没有一个单一的“触底”时刻，但我确实经历了一段走向破裂、在蜜月期就结束的婚姻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a series of pretty traumatic events for me in my privileged life.
zh: 在我这优越的人生里，我经历了一系列对我来说相当创伤性的事件。

speaker: Unknown
en: That ultimately made me realize, like, I can't keep living this way, but I don't know how to live.
zh: 这最终让我意识到，比如，我不能继续这样活下去了，但我不知道该怎么活。

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally was so broken that I was willing to raise my hand and ask for help.
zh: 最后我彻底崩溃了，才愿意举起手来寻求帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how I ended up in a treatment center.
zh: 我就是这样进了治疗中心的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happened in the hundred days there?
zh: 在那里的那一百天里发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the first thing that happened was that I was honest about what I was doing for the first time with someone else.
zh: 嗯，发生的头一件事是，我第一次对别人诚实地说明了我一直在做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I started sharing stories and things that I was doing.
zh: 我开始分享我的经历和我做过的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember a counselor, my counselor pulled me aside and said, you know, you like, you have a case of alcoholism that we typically only see in veteran drink, like people who are in their sixties, who've been doing this for a long time.
zh: 我记得一位咨询师，我的咨询师把我拉到一边说，你知道吗，你的酗酒病例，我们通常只在退伍老酒鬼身上见到，比如那些六十多岁、喝了很多年的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was 31 at the time.
zh: 而我当时才31岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he said, people like you die.
zh: 他还说，像你这样的人会死。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't get it, it's not gonna work out for you.
zh: 如果你不明白这一点，你是不会有好下场的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was able to hear that.
zh: 我最好的思考却把我送到了一个名义上算是、暂时性疯人院的地方，你知道吗，这非常令人羞愧，你知道吗，所以我被磨掉了傲气，我不仅能够寻求帮助，而且能够接受它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in my mind,
zh: 但在我心里，

speaker: Unknown
en: I was doing a spin dry.
zh: 我在做自我开脱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, this was bad, but I got things to do.
zh: 是啊，这很糟糕，但我还有事要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got to get back to my law firm job.
zh: 我得回到我律所的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when they said, you should stick around, I was like, I'll do it.
zh: 但当他们说，你应该留下来时，我说，行，我做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never want to come back here again.
zh: 我再也不想回到这里了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have an opportunity to completely wipe the slate clean and figure some things out about myself so that I don't have to come back here again.
zh: 我有一个机会把一切彻底清零，弄明白自己身上的一些问题，这样我就不必再回到这里了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was the recognition that
zh: 而我认识到了

speaker: Unknown
en: My best thinking, like I'm thinking, I'm this smart guy, you know, I've got in all these schools, I can do all these things.
zh: 我最好的思考，比如我自认为，我是这个聪明人，你知道吗，我进过所有这些学校，我能做这么多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: My best thinking landed me in what is ostensibly, you know, an asylum for the temporary, temporarily is insane, you know, and, and that was very humbling, you know, so I got humbled and I was able to not only ask for help, but, but receive it.
zh: 我最好的思考把我带到了一个表面上说是、你知道的、临时性的、暂时性的精神收容所，你知道的，而且，那是非常让人谦卑的，你知道的，所以我被谦卑了，我不仅能够寻求帮助，而且，能够接受帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interestingly, as a lawyer, maybe you'll be interested in this.
zh: 有意思的是，作为一个律师，也许你会对这个感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might want to cut it out because it's kind of an aside, but
zh: 你可能想把它剪掉，因为这有点跑题，但是

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I've ever told this story on a podcast.
zh: 我想我从来没在播客上讲过这个故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exclusive, exclusive first time I'm telling this.
zh: 独家，独家，我第一次讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before I went to that treatment center, I had been looking for another job and I had interviewed at a couple law firms.
zh: 在我去那个治疗中心之前，我一直在找别的工作，我在几家律所面试过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Aiken Gump was opening an office in Los Angeles.
zh: 当时 Aiken Gump 正在洛杉矶开设办公室。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I interviewed with Aiken Gump and they gave me an offer.
zh: 我面试了 Aiken Gump，他们给了我一个录用通知。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I went to rehab after they gave me the offer.
zh: 然后在他们给我录用通知之后，我去做了康复治疗。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I had told them that I was gonna go there.
zh: 而且我告诉过他们我要去那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm in treatment.
zh: 所以我在接受治疗。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd been there long enough that I had a clear mind.
zh: 我在那里待的时间够长，头脑已经清醒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said to my counselor, I was like, listen, I got this problem.
zh: 我对咨询师说，是这样，我有个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got a job offer from this other law firm, and I told them that I was going.
zh: 我拿到了另一家律所的工作录用，而且我告诉过他们我会去。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't know that I'm in this treatment center.
zh: 他们不知道我在这个治疗中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: What should I do?
zh: 我该怎么办？

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they said, well, you got to call and tell them, you know?
zh: 他们说，嗯，你得打电话告诉他们，你知道吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that was just terrifying.
zh: 那真是太可怕了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, of course, they're going to rescind the job offer.
zh: 就像，他们当然会撤回录用通知。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I had the counselor sit with me while I picked up the phone and like called them and I said, I know you offered me this job.
zh: 所以咨询师陪在我身边，我拿起电话给他们打了过去，我说，我知道你们给了我这份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: But here's the situation.
zh: 但情况是这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the guy, it was David Allen, it's a lawyer named David Allen.
zh: 而那个人，他叫 David Allen，是一位叫 David Allen 的律师。

speaker: Unknown
en: He goes, I'm gonna have to get back to you.
zh: 他说，我得再回复你。

speaker: Unknown
en: I said, okay.
zh: 我说，好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get back to me and miraculously, they're like, you still have a job here.
zh: 他们回复了我，奇迹般地，他们说，你在这里仍然有这份工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, wow, okay.
zh: 我当时就想，哇，好吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we're assigning you to this partner who's also in the program.
zh: 但是我们要把你分配给一位同样在这个项目里的合作伙伴。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I did a call with him.
zh: 于是我和他打了一通电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they said, well, we need you to get working on this case right now.
zh: 然后他们说，嗯，我们需要你现在就开始处理这个案子。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know you're in treatment, but we're gonna ship you all these files and these documents, you know, and you gotta start working.
zh: 我们知道你在接受治疗，但我们会把这些文件和文档都发给你，你知道的，你得开始干活了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need you to get going on this.
zh: 我们需要你马上着手处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my counselor was like, no f***ing way.
zh: 而我的咨询师说，绝对不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is not part of the protocol.
zh: 这不属于治疗规程的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, this is not, this is not going to work.
zh: 是啊，这不行，这样是行不通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I had to call them and say, I'm sorry, but I can't, I can't do that.
zh: 于是我不得不打电话给他们说，很抱歉，我不能，我不能那么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got to get this sobriety thing sorted out.
zh: 我得先把戒酒这件事搞定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the job went away then, but it was a sliding door moment.
zh: 于是那份工作就没了，但那是一个「命运的岔路口」时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I could have ended up as a lawyer.
zh: 你知道的，我本来可能会成为一名律师。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was in DC recently and I was riding a bike around and I rode by the Aiken Gump office and I was like, oh my God, like I could have been like living a completely different life.
zh: 我最近在华盛顿特区，骑着自行车到处逛，路过 Aiken Gump 的办公室时，我心想，天哪，我本来可能过着一种完全不同的人生。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I was introduced to these new tools for living and these spiritual principles and I returned to Los Angeles and just made sobriety my number one priority.
zh: 但我接触到了这些全新的生活工具和这些灵性原则，我回到了洛杉矶，把保持清醒（sobriety）列为我的头等大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I returned to the law firm where I was working, but really my job was creating a solid foundation of sobriety and I immersed myself in the recovery community of Los Angeles.
zh: 我回到了我工作的那家律所，但实际上我的工作是打下坚实的清醒基础，我全身心投入到了洛杉矶的康复社群中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm struck by how out of integrity you were at the time and how much integrity is central to your life and your work now.
zh: 让我很触动的是，你当时是多么地不诚信（out of integrity），而现在诚信又是多么地成为你生活和工作的核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you continue on the journey to integrity and leave the law and end up on that organic farm in Hawaii?
zh: 你是如何在通往诚信的旅程上继续前行，离开法律行业，最终去了夏威夷那个有机农场的？

speaker: Unknown
en: It took a very long time.
zh: 这花了很长很长的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if you Google me, it might sound like I got sober and then I started running ultra marathons and I had a podcast.
zh: 我想如果你谷歌我，听起来可能像是我戒了酒，然后就开始跑超级马拉松，还开了播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was not like that at all.
zh: 完全不是那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I went back and worked at that law firm.
zh: 我回去在那家律所工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I committed myself to...
zh: 我全身心投入到……

speaker: Unknown
en: I knew I couldn't stay there.
zh: 我知道我不能一直待在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I knew...
zh: 我知道……

speaker: Unknown
en: Emerging from treatment, I knew like this law firm life is not for me.
zh: 从治疗中走出来的时候，我就知道，这种律所生活不适合我。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been jamming a square peg into a round hole forever.
zh: 我只是一直在被动地按照一个程序生活着。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't even know who I am.
zh: 我甚至不知道自己是谁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've just been living my life reactively based upon a program.
zh: 我一直只是被动地按照一个程序在生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I need to figure out
zh: 我需要弄清楚

speaker: Unknown
en: Who I am, who I want to be, what's important to me.
zh: 我是谁，我想成为什么样的人，什么对我来说是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: These were questions I never asked myself until I got sober.
zh: 这些是我直到戒酒之前从未问过自己的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I didn't have immediate solutions to those programs and I needed to pay the bills.
zh: 而这真的加速了我重新思考自己与职业和专业之间关系的进程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I stayed at this law firm for a while.
zh: 所以我在这家律所又待了一段时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ultimately, I left because I just couldn't, I was like, I couldn't even type a confirmation letter anymore.
zh: 最终，我离开了，因为我实在受不了了，我心想，我连一封确认函都打不动了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like some might say it was burnout, but I think it was really just, I'm so out of integrity being here.
zh: 有人可能会说那是职业倦怠，但我认为那其实真的就是，我在这里的诚信缺失太严重了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, not that it's, there's anything wrong with being a lawyer in a law firm.
zh: 倒不是说，当律师、在律所工作有什么不对。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just, it wasn't, it wasn't what I was supposed to be doing.
zh: 只是那不是，那不是我应该做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I knew that to my core.
zh: 我从骨子里知道这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was on the precipice of turning 40 and I had a health scare and that kind of collided with this existential crisis that I was having.
zh: 我即将年满 40 岁，又遇到了一次健康危机，这和我正在经历的存在危机撞在了一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And
zh: 而

speaker: Unknown
en: I had an experience not unlike hitting bottom with alcoholism where I realized I needed to make some lifestyle changes.
zh: 我有过一次和酒精成瘾触底时很相似的经历，我意识到我需要改变一些生活方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that really kind of accelerated the trajectory of rethinking my relationship with career and profession.
zh: 而这真的在某种程度上加速了我重新思考我与职业和专业之间关系的轨迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I understand it, you committed to an Ultraman competition before you started training.
zh: 据我所知，你在开始训练之前就报名承诺参加了一场 Ultraman 比赛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I have that right?
zh: 我说得对吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not quite that, yeah.
zh: 不完全是这样，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I had started exercising again because I changed my diet and I felt revitalized.
zh: 我是说，我重新开始锻炼了，因为我改变了饮食，感觉焕发了活力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I'd been basically eating fast food and Chinese food in the law firm and had gained a bunch of weight.
zh: 你知道的，在律所的时候我基本上吃的就是快餐和中餐，体重增加了不少。

speaker: Unknown
en: I started taking care of myself and I had this resurgence of energy and...
zh: 我开始照顾好自己，精力也重新涌了上来，然后……

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I went back to the pool and my wife got me a bike for my birthday and I started a little bit of running and, you know, I'm 40 now.
zh: 你知道的，我回到了游泳池，我妻子送了我一辆自行车作为生日礼物，我开始跑一点步，你知道的，我现在 40 岁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what do you do when you're 40?
zh: 那么你 40 岁的时候做什么呢？
